architecture: README.md:77-104 — the layer table (runtime, protocol, JSON, values, storage, lexer/parser, semantic analysis, logical plan, optimizer, physical planning, planning driver, execution, vectorized execution, parallelism, server) matches the src/ tree: one .S file per concern, 41 modules
README.md:837-853 and optimize.S:1-28,39-60 — CR-3 module map is accurate. optimize() walks a rule table of LogicalNode*->LogicalNode* functions, with one rule_*.S module per rule

logical.S:56 lp_build, physical.S:62 phys_plan / :83 pp_lower, access.S:512 ap_scan / :724 scan_estimate, plan.S:38 plan_statement / :210 plan_explain — the entry points the README names exist in the modules it puts them in
lexer.S:1-21 and parser.S:20-36 — lexing (token array, lexer.inc) is a separate stage from recursive-descent parsing, which has its own error and limit contract
protocol.S:1-12,397-470 — handle_request is transport independent: one table-driven op dispatch, catalog read/write mode per op. http.S:14-17 routes every endpoint through it
catalog.S:1-31,174-257 — the versioned, ref-counted catalog (snapshot isolation) is isolated behind cat_read_begin/cat_write_begin/cat_end
include/API.md:1-80 — internal API contract per module (inputs, outputs, raises), with shared structures centralized in include/pq.inc

Weakness: physical.S:183 pp_rewrite, :255 push_conj, :318 pp_joins repeat the conjunct placement that rule_pushdown.S does (README.md:875-886 justifies this for optimize:false). Large multi-concern files: pqcf.S 2972 lines (writer, reader and CRC/UTF-8 helpers), binder.S 2591, http.S 2557
readability: include/frame.inc:1-57 — ENTER/LEAVE/LEAVE_NORET macros generate AAPCS64 frame records and callee-saved pairs with guaranteed 16-byte alignment. Used about 386 times across the modules

include/pq.inc:27-102 — FUNC/LFUNC/ENDF, ADR_L, LDR_G, TLS_ADDR/TLS_LDR (local-exec TLS), GOT_LOAD, RAISE and NOTE_GNU_STACK macros remove repeated boilerplate. pq.inc:14-21 documents conventions such as the value pair (x0 payload, x1 isnull)
lexer.S:171-179, vexec.S:136-142, optimize.S:36-38, server.S:225-227 — most routines have a header comment with signature and register allocation (e.g. 'x19 cursor x20 end of input ...')
json.S:16-24, ingest.S:11-12, index.S:857-861 — non-standard internal conventions (helpers that share the caller's x19..x26) are written down. My static scan found every such case documented
lexer.S:148-179 — small local macros (TRACK_TO_X27, IF_IDENT_CHAR) give names to recurring idioms. eval.S:453-485 is commented at the level of semantics ('INT64_MIN / -1 overflows')

Routine size: median about 34 lines over 705 routines, but some are very long: vexec.S:143 veval about 755 lines, functions.S ev_func about 426, lexer.S:180 lex_tokenize about 398, sort.S rsort_rows about 336

Inconsistent style: rt.S, protocol.S (45 occurrences) and parser.S write prologues by hand (stp x29,x30 ...) where most modules use ENTER. vexec.S:469-475 and pqcf.S:2524 use bl-called local subroutines that push x30 but do not set x29
robustness: ABI: a static scan of all 1410 FUNC/LFUNC bodies found no routine with ENTER n using a callee-saved register above x(18+2n). The one hit, http.S:2534-2536 wait_idle, only reads the caller's x21 and says so. No x18/w18 anywhere in src/. d8 is saved and restored in rt.S:782-808, and no other module touches d8-d15 or v8-v15. No odd-multiple-of-8 SP adjustments found

rt.S:1-8,267-277 and protocol.S:397-478 — setjmp/longjmp error model. All per-request memory is in g_arena, freed on every path. On error: the pending table is freed, catalog changes are discarded (cat_end 0), a structured error is emitted

rule_fold.S:127-169, parallel.S:556-598, pqcf.S:455-467 — nested error handlers save and restore the 512-byte g_jmpbuf, so constant folding, inline tasks and temp-file cleanup can intercept errors and recover

server.S:262-349 — every pq_raise in admission control comes after srv_unlock (no lock held across longjmp). The queue wait uses a bounded 10 ms cond_timedwait that re-checks cancellation and deadline (server.S:355-395)

rt.S:296-318 — per-request memory budget (RESOURCE_LIMIT) and malloc-failure handling in arena_alloc_in. pq.inc:105-122 has a complete error-code table. rt.S:42-48 sets default ingest, row and join limits

parser.S:33-36,102-118 — PARSE_MAX_DEPTH 256 recursion guard. json.S:29,561,590 — JSON_MAX_DEPTH 1000. http.S:2384-2391 — 16 MiB connection-thread stacks. http.S:49-62,1683-1685,1881 — limits on head size, target length and chunk-line length

pqcf.S:27-38,2082-2101,2476-2520 — the PQCF reader checks header, footer, CRCs, chunk offset/length (overflow-safe subtraction form), minimum sizes, RLE run counts and offsets before using any of it, and raises STORAGE_CORRUPT

eval.S:453-485 — INT64 + - * / % with overflow checks (adds/b.vs, smulh sign-extension test, INT64_MIN/-1, x % -1). vexec.S:322,743 reuses the same checks. vagg.S:1182-1183,2232-2234 accumulates SUM in 128 or 192 bits

Weaknesses: catalog.S:118-121 (cv_clone) and server.S:306-310 (calloc) call abort() on out-of-memory, a crash path. rt.S:284-291 does no overflow check on allocation sizes. Per-task memory budget under parallelism (see suspected defects)
testability: Makefile:12-36 — make test builds and runs every tests/unit/test_*.S, each linked against all engine objects except main.o, then runs tests/sh/*.sh. Adding a test file is picked up automatically by wildcard
tests/unit — 13 assembly unit-test programs (about 8.5k lines): rt, json, values, parser, binder, catalog, ingest, storage, pqcf, functions, plan, optimizer, exec5

tests/unit/test_optimizer.S:19-45 — table-driven case macros (TO/TOFF/PL/TEND) with hand-built in-memory tables (:48-77). A new case is a few lines of SQL plus the expected plan text. README.md:868-873 reports 42 cases, one per rule
tests/unit/test_exec5.S:1-19 — differential cases: each SQL runs under six execution settings with g_par_min_rows=1 to force parallel tasks, checking row count and an order-independent checksum
tests/sh/run_mode_tests.sh:1-30 — option-matrix (mode x join x threads x optimize) differential test, with HTTP, CLI, storage, sort and decimal38 shell suites alongside
Verification aids: PQ_TRACE_PLAN (optimize.S:26-27; logical.S:315 lp_print), PQ_TRACE_PAR (parallel.S:121-125,198-218), PQ_POOL_SPIN, and the lint target that checks .note.GNU-stack (Makefile:38-43)

Gaps: no direct unit tests for http.S, server.S, sort.S, index.S or the lexer as a separate unit (covered only indirectly or through shell tests). run_mode_tests.sh:8-12 quietly skips when the fixtures outside the engine directory are missing

top_strengths: Clean layered architecture that matches its README: separate lexer, parser, binder, logical plan, rule-per-module optimizer, physical planner, row/vectorized/parallel executors, storage, protocol and server, plus a written internal API contract (include/API.md)

Disciplined AAPCS64 practice: frame macros, documented per-routine register allocation, documented custom conventions for internal helpers, no x18 use, d8 saved where used. A static scan found no ENTER-depth/callee-saved mismatches

Thorough defensive handling: setjmp/longjmp errors with arena-based cleanup and nested handlers, depth/size/memory limits, a fully validating PQCF reader, overflow-checked integer arithmetic, unlock before every raise in server code
Table-driven assembly unit tests plus differential execution-mode tests and trace environment variables make the engine checkable despite being written in assembly
top_weaknesses: Some very long routines (veval about 755 lines, ev_func about 426, lex_tokenize about 398) that are hard to review
Two prologue styles (hand-written stp vs ENTER) and local bl-subroutines that do not maintain the x29 frame chain
Conjunct-placement logic repeated in the physical planner (physical.S) and the pushdown rule (rule_pushdown.S)
abort() on out-of-memory in catalog cloning and query registration, and no overflow guards on allocation sizes
No unit tests for the HTTP server, admission control, sort or index modules. The mode differential test depends on fixtures outside the engine directory

suspected_defects.description: UNVERIFIED. Each pool task gets a copy of the caller's full g_arena_limit and starts with a fresh, empty arena, so the per-query memory budget applies per task, not to the query. Before arena_adopt merges the arenas (parallel.S:221-230), peak memory can reach about (tasks+1) x max_query_mem.

UNVERIFIED. arena_alloc_in rounds (add #15) and bump-adds the size without overflow checks. A size near 2^64 (for example from an unchecked count*width multiply in a caller) would wrap to a small allocation and could overflow the heap. Likely unreachable given the row limits, but there is no guard.

UNVERIFIED. Out-of-memory in cv_clone, or calloc failure while registering a query, calls abort(), which kills the whole server process instead of returning RESOURCE_LIMIT. The cv_clone case is intentional per its comment.

UNVERIFIED, minor. Worker and inline-task error messages are copied into a 256-byte WK_MSG buffer, while g_err_msg holds 1024 bytes (rt.S:12), so a long error message raised in a parallel task may be truncated differently from the same error in row or single-thread mode.

UNVERIFIED, low impact. Local subroutines reached by bl push x29/x30 but do not set x29 = sp, so the frame-record chain is incomplete inside them. This affects only debugger and unwinder backtraces, not correctness.
